Affiliation:: The University of Oklahoma, Department of Psychology
Research Domains: Phenomenological Variant of Ecological Systems Theory (PVEST)
Techniques Used: Pre-Post Test Design without Control Group
Data & Platforms: U.S. High School Educator Interview Data
U.S. High School Student Survey Data (N=180)
Application Areas: Youth Psychosocial Well-being and Academic Adjustment
Culturally Sustaining Pedagogy and Teacher Professional Development
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Intensive Longitudinal Process Modeling: Capturing real-time within-person dynamics of identity and discrimination through Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) and daily diary data to understand moment-to-moment psychological consequences.

Developmental Cascade Systems Analysis: Utilizing chain sequential mediation analyses and bias-corrected bootstrapping to map how ethnic-racial identity development cascades into broader psychosocial adjustment and academic outcomes over time.

Translational Implementation Science: Evaluating the fidelity and effectiveness of scaling up evidence-based curricula like the Identity Project by training teachers as delivery agents, thereby bridging the gap between theoretical intervention design and practical school-based dissemination.

Mixed-Methods Ecological Inquiry: Integrating Consensual Qualitative Research (CQR) and semi-structured focus groups with quantitative survey data to contextualize ethnic-racial identity development within specific cultural-ecological systems, such as Colombian and U.S. adolescent populations.
Summary Description: Michael R. Sladek is a developmental psychologist specializing in ethnic-racial identity (ERI) development, prevention science, and implementation science. His research bridges theoretical models of identity formation with practical, teacher-led dissemination strategies in K-12 settings. Utilizing intensive longitudinal methods like EMA and developmental cascade modeling, he investigates how ERI shapes youth psychosocial adjustment and academic engagement in real-time. A key focus is the translational efficacy of the Identity Project, assessing how teacher delivery impacts culturally sustaining pedagogy and addresses ethnic-racial mismatch. By combining qualitative ecological inquiry with rigorous quantitative mediation analyses, Sladek enhances the external validity of identity research, providing actionable insights for promoting mental health and equity in marginalized contexts.
